title: Prefetch-aware windowed scheduler tuning and client fairness shaping
author: Maya Patel
release_notes: Introduce a prefetch-aware windowed admission policy and client-weighted fairness shaping on the continuous batcher. Default gated behind feature flag 'prefetch_windowed_scheduler'. Improvements: lower P95/P99 tail, fewer KV cold-misses, smoother throughput under skewed clients.
description:
Context and motivation: In production we continue to see head-of-line blocking when a small number of KV-cold, heavy requests occupy batcher slots during continuous batching windows. This increases tail latency for small/short requests and drives up token cost due to repeated KV misses. This PR implements a windowed admission layer that is prefetch-aware and a client-weighted fairness shaper to reduce starvation and improve SLO adherence.

What this change does (high level): Adds a new 'PrefetchWindowedScheduler' that slices continuous-batcher admission into short windows (configurable, default 12ms) and tracks per-window expected kernel cost and KV-warmth hints. The scheduler: (1) prefers admitting requests that have KV-warmup hints or low expected kernel cost to reduce head-of-line blocking; (2) enforces a client token-bucket so noisy neighbors cannot consume all window slots; (3) emits soft-preemption signals for requests that exceed a configurable 'kindly-yield' timer so the batcher can reshuffle without hard-killing; (4) propagates KV-warmup hint metadata into the KV layer so prefetchers can warm embeddings/kv entries ahead of scheduling.

Implementation notes: - runtime/scheduler/prefetch_windowed_scheduler.go: new scheduler implementation with admission windows, per-client token buckets, and yield timers. - runtime/kv/cache_warmup_hint.cc + .h: C++ side hook to accept warmup hints and touch hot-keys without blocking main path. - runtime/bench/bench_prefetch_scheduler.py: added microbench harness to measure windowed admission effects. - runtime/metrics/scheduler_metrics.go: new metrics (window_slots_offered, warmup_hit_rate, kindly_yield_count). - configs/flags.yaml: feature flag prefetched_window_scheduler (off by default) and tuning knobs.

Design trade-offs: We intentionally keep windows short to avoid added admission latency; longer windows improve batching efficiency but increase H/o-L blocking risk. The client token bucket is leaky and decays reservation slowly to avoid lock-in. Soft preemption is cooperative: kernels need to support quick checkpoint/yield for long lived requests — fallback is still safe because we don't preempt work mid-kernel.

Benchmarks (perf-lab; representative load with mixed short/long requests): - Baseline (continuous-batcher vX): 95th latency = 380ms, 99th = 630ms, KV miss rate = 18% - With feature on (default knobs): 95th latency = 335ms (-12%), 99th = 565ms (-10%), KV miss rate = 12% (-33%), sustained throughput +7% before SLO degradation. Token cost per 1M tokens down ~6%. Microbench harness attached for reproducibility.

Testing: - Unit tests for windowing and token-bucket logic. - Integration tests exercising KV warmup hook (simulated cold-hit and warm-hit) in bench cluster. - Load tests across perf-canary with feature flag ramp: 10% -> 25% -> 50% -> 100%. All stages passed; two reruns needed for a flaky bench job that was unrelated (disk image pull timeout).

Rollout plan: Gate behind feature flag (off by default). Start 10% on perf-canary, observe warmup_hit_rate and kindly_yield_count, then follow canary ramp. If any regression >5% on 99th latency, auto rollback.

Checklist: - [x] Scheduler implementation - [x] KV warmup hook - [x] Metrics + dashboards - [x] Bench harness + reproducible numbers - [x] Unit and integration tests - [x] Documentation: runtime/ops/README.md updated with knobs and troubleshooting notes.

Related work: builds on previous fairshare/cohort batching efforts but focuses on prefetch coordination with KV cache and cooperative yield rather than hard preemption. Linear refs: ENG-2345 (kernel affinity hints), ENG-2411 (kv warmup roadmap).

Notes for reviewers: Focus review on the admission loop and token decay math; the yield-handling path must not drop kernel state. Prefetch hooks are opt-in and non-blocking by design.

review_comments: Ethan Rios: Nice direction. Two requests: (1) add a small linearizability test for token decay when multiple clients burst; (2) clarify how kindly-yield interacts with time-sliced kernels.

Maya Patel (author): Added unit test for token decay and extended doc comments on yield interaction; kindly-yield triggers a cooperative checkpoint request, not a hard interrupt — clarified in comments.
Claire Nguyen: Benchmark numbers look promising. Can we add an experiment where prefetch hints are noisy (false positives) to show robustness?
Maya Patel (author): Added bench scenario 'warmup_false_positive' and verified regression is <1% on throughput; added to bench scripts.
Omar Haddad: LGTM after one nit: use exponential backoff for token bucket refill when a client is repeatedly throttled to avoid oscillation.
